title: Five ways to organize nodes inside an Expanded Block
brief: Make a selected set of child Blocks organize coherently inside a fixed Expanded parent, while allowing the parent’s input/output ports to influence placement. The same run() fixture is used throughout: raw, gain, and Estimator enter from the parent boundary; decode → transform → encode carries the interior flow; bytes exits through the parent boundary.
defaultWhy: Paired Boundary Rails is the provisional choice at 91/100. It captures the user's virtual-parent instinct at the right abstraction: not a persisted fake Block and not an ELK-owned compound, but two disposable boundary representatives inside the existing flat solve. The installed elkjs 0.12.0 probe accepts fixed rail-port positions, lays out the child graph cleanly, and fits the representative frame; a post-solve bounds guard closes the remaining safety gap.
decisionHinge: The hinge is whether exact boundary-row residuals deserve their own solver. Move five weight points from Implementation fit to Boundary-port legibility and V4 ELK + Vertical Reconciler leads 92 to 90. Keep V1 unless repeated evaluation shows that the rail model leaves visibly avoidable doglegs; then splice V4's row-residual pass and diagnostics onto V1 rather than adopting a compound parent.
invariants: Expanded is a free tldraw frame: organizing children never moves or resizes the parent and never resizes descendants.
Geometry is not parenthood. The real parentId chain and connection scopeId decide which parent boundary participates.
The parent boundary is the invariant; Simple, Port, and Expanded are projections of the same stable port identities.
Only selected child Blocks move. Unselected siblings, nested descendants, parent ports, and cables remain document-identical.
ELK chooses positions only. SystemSketch's existing connection router remains the sole owner of painted cable geometry.
Exact simultaneous alignment is impossible when a child's port-to-port spacing differs from the corresponding parent-row spacing; ordering is hard, row straightness is optimized.
boundary: Architecture prototype, not a production behavior change. The data-contract inspection and two elkjs 0.12.0 probes are executable against the current repository; the five visual outcomes, selection grouping, overflow message, and any second-stage optimization remain proposed. Prior decisions were recovered from the PyBlocks recursive-boundary, expanded-membership, and layout-command reports plus the current SystemSketch parentId/inner-face/organizeGraph implementation.

requirements.name: Boundary-port legibility
requirements.why: The parent boundary is the stable interface. Its input/output identities and row order should visibly influence the interior arrangement.
requirements.passCondition: The run() fixture produces short, ordered boundary runs and never permutes raw, gain, Estimator, or bytes.

anchors.1: Parent ports are ignored or reordered.
anchors.3: The boundary influences broad direction, but several avoidable doglegs remain.
anchors.5: Port order is exact and the solver minimizes row error wherever the geometry permits.

requirements.name: Interior topology readability
requirements.why: Boundary alignment is not useful if decode → transform → encode becomes longer, crossed, or overlapping.
requirements.passCondition: The selected child graph remains left-to-right, non-overlapping, and no more crossed than the current ELK result.

anchors.1: Boundary placement dominates and damages the child graph.
anchors.3: The main path reads, with visible detours or weak packing.
anchors.5: The full child topology and its port offsets remain first-class solver inputs.

requirements.name: Semantic fidelity
requirements.why: A virtual parent is useful only as a layout device; SystemSketch's real parentId, Block IDs, binding faces, and routing authority must remain canonical.
requirements.passCondition: The solve persists only positions for selected child Blocks; no proxy shape, proxy binding, or ELK route enters the document.

anchors.1: The proposal adds persisted fake Blocks or competes with tldraw containment/routing.
anchors.3: It is mostly transient but duplicates meaningful document semantics.
anchors.5: Every virtual object is a disposable adapter over existing canonical records.

requirements.name: Fixed-frame safety
requirements.why: Expanded is a free frame: organizing its contents must not silently resize the Block or clip children beyond frameInterior.
requirements.passCondition: All moved child bounds fit the existing drawable interior; an infeasible solve is a no-op with a clear capacity result.

anchors.1: The parent resizes or children silently overflow.
anchors.3: Common cases fit, but overflow behavior is heuristic.
anchors.5: Fit is validated as a hard postcondition with a deterministic failure path.

requirements.name: Implementation fit
requirements.why: The safest port should extend organizeGraph and reuse ELK 0.12.0, not introduce a second persistent graph or general constraint engine.
requirements.passCondition: The design is a narrow adapter around collectOrganizeEdges, organizeGraph, layoutBlock.frameInterior, and editor.updateShapes.

anchors.1: Requires a broad new solver or changes the canvas model.
anchors.3: Adds a bounded but substantial placement subsystem.
anchors.5: Extends the existing graph adapter and validation seam with small, isolated types.

hardGates.name: Selection and frame stay fixed
hardGates.why: Only selected child Blocks move; parent geometry and unselected shapes are immutable.

hardGates.name: Virtual means ephemeral
hardGates.why: No rail, satellite, or parent surrogate may become a tldraw record or serialized ID.

hardGates.name: Ports and routing stay canonical
hardGates.why: Bindings retain exact portId/inner-face semantics and SystemSketch remains the sole cable router.

hardGates.name: No silent overflow
hardGates.why: Every real child must fit frameInterior after the solve, otherwise the command must leave the scope unchanged.

hardGates.name: One containment scope per solve
hardGates.why: Only the immediate expanded parent and connections whose scopeId equals that parent participate; nested scopes solve independently.

variants.name: Paired Boundary Rails
variants.thesis: Represent the parent as two tall, layout-only nodes—one input rail and one output rail—whose fixed-position ports mirror the parent’s inner-face rows.
variants.bestWhen: The parent frame is fixed, several boundary ports should influence one child graph, and the existing ELK adapter should remain the only layout engine.
variants.losesWhen: Exact straight-through alignment is mandatory for every boundary cable, even when parent-row spacing and child-port spacing are geometrically incompatible.

decisions.label: Virtual object
decisions.value: Two zero-thickness rail nodes, with exact parent-local port coordinates and fixed order.

decisions.label: Solve
decisions.value: Run one flat ELK graph containing selected children, internal edges, rails, and parent-boundary edges.

decisions.label: Commit
decisions.value: Discard rails and ELK routes, translate real children into frameInterior, validate fit, then update only selected Blocks.

keepParts: exact parent port IDs and row order
proof: An executable elkjs 0.12.0 probe on this fixture returned 1042×393 with zero graph padding; every real child fit a 1120×390 interior and the input rail stayed at (0,0).
The same probe preserved each supplied rail port coordinate and placed decode → transform → encode left-to-right without overlap.
The output rail drifted 3 px vertically, which is harmless only because the rail is discarded and confirms that boundary straightness must be an objective, not an exact global-position promise.

fr1.evidence: The live probe keeps exact rail-port order and lets all four parent edges influence the solve; not every cable becomes straight because one child translation cannot satisfy incompatible row gaps.

fr2.evidence: Boundary and child edges share one layered solve, preserving the complete decode → transform → encode topology and fixed child-port offsets.

fr3.evidence: Rails exist only in the ELK input/output adapter; only real child x/y values survive.

fr4.evidence: The measured fixture fits, and a required post-solve validator makes overflow safe; ELK itself does not enforce the exact frame rectangle.

fr5.evidence: This is a bounded extension of OrganizeGraphNode and collectOrganizeEdges using the already installed ELK engine.

g1.evidence: Rails are fixed context; the commit list contains selected child IDs only.

g2.evidence: Synthetic IDs are namespaced inside the call and discarded before editor.updateShapes().

g3.evidence: Each rail port projects an existing parent portId/inner binding; returned ELK sections are ignored.

g4.evidence: The direction includes a hard frameInterior bounds check and no-op result for infeasible layouts.

g5.evidence: One rail pair is synthesized per immediate expanded-parent scope; nested scopes are separate calls.

variants.name: Literal Compound Parent
variants.thesis: Mirror the Expanded Block directly as an ELK compound node, place selected children beneath it, and attach cross-hierarchy edges to its real boundary ports.
variants.bestWhen: The layout engine is allowed to own container size and port redistribution, as in an auto-sizing diagram rather than a user-sized whiteboard frame.
variants.losesWhen: The existing parent rectangle and port rows are authored geometry that must remain byte-identical.

decisions.label: Virtual object
decisions.value: One compound ELK node with real selected children and parent ports.

decisions.label: Solve
decisions.value: Set hierarchyHandling=INCLUDE_CHILDREN and let ELK Layered process cross-hierarchy edges.

decisions.label: Commit
decisions.value: Accept the compound result, including the container geometry ELK believes is required.

proof: elkjs 0.12.0 successfully routed parent-port → child-port edges with hierarchyHandling=INCLUDE_CHILDREN.
In the executable probe, ELK rewrote the supplied parent from 1120×460 to 784×194 and moved the parent ports from y=108/205 to y=66.
That is valid ELK compound behavior but violates SystemSketch's expanded-frame contract, so this direction is ineligible as stated.

fr1.evidence: Cross-hierarchy edges are understood, but ELK moved the authored parent rows to suit its computed compound size.

fr2.evidence: The compound graph gives ELK complete topology and produces a clean left-to-right child chain.

fr3.evidence: The compound is still a projection, but accepting its output would duplicate and overwrite meaningful frame geometry.

fr4.evidence: The measured probe shrank 1120×460 to 784×194 despite supplied dimensions, directly failing the fixed-frame contract.

fr5.evidence: ELK supports the feature, but reconciling its compound size/ports with stock tldraw frames would require custom post-processing.

g1.evidence: The executable probe changed parent width, height, and port rows.

g2.evidence: The compound surrogate can remain in-memory only.

g3.evidence: The test used exact parent and child port IDs and ignored ELK routes at commit.

g4.evidence: ELK solved by resizing the compound boundary rather than proving the children fit the authored frame.

g5.evidence: INCLUDE_CHILDREN can be limited to one immediate parent scope.

variants.name: Port Satellites
variants.thesis: Create one tiny virtual terminal for every connected parent port and tie the terminals together with an ordering spine, rather than representing the whole boundary.
variants.bestWhen: Only a sparse subset of parent ports is connected and each terminal should exert independent pressure on the child topology.
variants.losesWhen: Many ports turn the hidden ordering spine into another graph whose spacing and crossing behavior must be tuned and tested.

decisions.label: Virtual object
decisions.value: One disposable zero-area node per used boundary port.

decisions.label: Ordering
decisions.value: A hidden north-to-south spine or model-order constraint prevents ELK from permuting satellites.

decisions.label: Commit
decisions.value: Discard satellites/spine, fit-check children, and update selected IDs only.

proof: Every used parent port becomes a separate, inspectable force in the layout graph.
Unlike a rail, the satellites have no intrinsic common height, so preserving parent row gaps requires an additional invisible ordering/spacing structure.
The proxy count grows linearly with connected parent ports and remains fully ephemeral.

fr1.evidence: Each boundary port has a distinct proxy and exact identity, but an auxiliary spine is required to preserve authored ordering and approximate gaps.

fr2.evidence: All topology remains in ELK, though extra proxy edges can influence layering and crossing minimization more than the semantic graph warrants.

fr3.evidence: Satellites and their spine are disposable adapter records with no persisted counterpart.

fr4.evidence: A post-solve frame check makes the result safe; the proxies themselves do not encode the full rectangular capacity.

fr5.evidence: The adapter is local, but order-spine generation and its tuning add more graph machinery than two rails.

g1.evidence: Only selected child IDs reach the update list.

g2.evidence: Every satellite/spine ID is synthetic and discarded.

g3.evidence: Each satellite maps one existing parent portId and never supplies persisted routing.

g4.evidence: The direction adopts the same hard frameInterior postcondition as V1.

g5.evidence: Satellites are synthesized only from edges scoped to the immediate parent.

variants.name: ELK + Vertical Reconciler
variants.thesis: Let the current child-only ELK solve topology first, then run a bounded vertical optimization that minimizes parent-port row error while enforcing non-overlap and frame bounds.
variants.bestWhen: Boundary-row quality is worth a dedicated numerical objective and the team accepts a small second solver with explicit priorities.
variants.losesWhen: A single understandable layout engine and predictable debugging matter more than squeezing the last dogleg out of a boundary-heavy graph.

decisions.label: Virtual object
decisions.value: No fake node; parent-port rows become weighted equations over each connected child's y translation.

decisions.label: Solve
decisions.value: ELK topology first, then constrained 1-D projection for row error, separation, and frame bounds.

decisions.label: Conflict
decisions.value: When exact rows disagree, minimize weighted error without changing child port spacing.

proof: The model can state the actual impossibility: one child translation cannot simultaneously match two parent row gaps that differ from its own port gap.
The preview separates the ELK proposal (dashed) from the reconciled positions (solid), making the second solver's ownership visible.
No existing dependency provides this exact bounded objective, so the critical algorithm remains a prototype rather than executed production evidence.

fr1.evidence: Every parent edge contributes a measurable row-residual term, and incompatible targets degrade explicitly rather than being silently ignored.

fr2.evidence: ELK chooses topology first, but the reconciliation pass can bend its carefully optimized vertical alignment and must recheck crossings.

fr3.evidence: The second pass consumes canonical geometry and returns child positions only; no proxy semantics exist.

fr4.evidence: Interior bounds and non-overlap are direct hard constraints rather than an after-the-fact heuristic.

fr5.evidence: It introduces and must validate a new constrained optimizer, priority policy, and infeasibility diagnostics beside ELK.

g1.evidence: The variables are y translations for selected children only.

g2.evidence: There are no virtual document or layout nodes.

g3.evidence: The equations reference canonical port coordinates; cable geometry still comes from SystemSketch.

g4.evidence: Bounds and non-overlap are hard constraints in the proposed optimization.

g5.evidence: Each optimization is built from one immediate scope and its parent-inner bindings.

variants.name: Boundary-First Lanes
variants.thesis: Treat parent input rows as horizontal lanes, seed boundary-connected children into those lanes, then pack the remaining topology between the seeded islands.
variants.bestWhen: The drawing is read primarily from the parent API inward and stable visual lanes matter more than globally compact graph layout.
variants.losesWhen: One child consumes several parent inputs, components cross lanes, or deep interior topology should determine the vertical order instead.

decisions.label: Virtual object
decisions.value: Horizontal lane bands derived from parent port rows, not graph nodes.

decisions.label: Solve
decisions.value: Anchor boundary-connected components first; run packing/layout inside and between their allocated bands.

decisions.label: Conflict
decisions.value: A multi-input child joins the dominant lane and other inputs bend into it.

proof: The preview makes the parent's public interface dominant and gives raw, gain, and Estimator stable horizontal territories.
The transform Block spans several inputs, exposing the arbitrary dominant-lane decision rather than hiding it.
This is a custom packing policy, not a configuration of the current flat ELK adapter.

fr1.evidence: Parent rows are the explicit organizing structure and remain visibly ordered.

fr2.evidence: Simple pipelines read well, but multi-lane children and cross-lane edges can fragment the semantic graph.

fr3.evidence: Lanes are calculated presentation guides and never become canvas records.

fr4.evidence: Lane allocation can respect the fixed interior, but dense graphs need an explicit infeasible/no-op policy.

fr5.evidence: The concept is bounded but requires a new lane allocator and component packer rather than a small ELK input adapter.

g1.evidence: Only selected children are assigned lanes or moved.

g2.evidence: Lane bands are transient calculations/overlays only.

g3.evidence: Lane membership derives from exact parent port IDs; SystemSketch still routes the edges.

g4.evidence: The proposal includes capacity calculation and no-op on dense infeasible scopes.

g5.evidence: Lanes are created from one immediate expanded parent at a time.

story.title: Lay out from the public boundary inward

steps.label: Find the parent API
steps.caption: The boundary rows already state the external reading order, but the tangled children do not respect it.

steps.label: Seed port-owned lanes
steps.caption: The colored bands reserve that order; topology is packed within them and bends resolve multi-lane conflicts.

media.label: Outside-in packing trace
media.caption: The boundary becomes visually primary, but the dominant-lane rule is a new policy users may have to learn.
media.html:
parent rows→lane bands→seed connected children→pack remaining components→validate capacity

A child attached to two or more lanes cannot live in all of them; one lane wins and the remaining edges bend.

checks: Exactly five structurally distinct virtual-parent/layout models
Same run() frame, boundary ports, child Blocks, and messy starting geometry in every hero
Five frozen weighted criteria sum to 100; every score includes evidence and confidence
Five hard gates are evaluated separately; the literal compound direction visibly fails two
Every hero has a direct before/result toggle and a guided two-step story over those same states
Every direction includes an architecture trace, concrete commit boundary, and failure policy
The recommended direction is supported by an isolated live elkjs 0.12.0 probe, not only a drawing
Pick, shortlist, reject, note, splice, copy, and download remain available in the gallery
No production SystemSketch behavior or document record was changed by this exploration
